style_prompt:
Style: Warm, curious Alaska public-radio register. Genuine admiration for the engineering, honest about an unconfirmed rollout. Never sour, never boosterish, never smug. The stretch on the fair case for patience gets real warmth, not a setup for a gotcha; if that tone slips the piece breaks. Dry wit only where the facts earn it, like the beat on 'no number anywhere.' The two verbatim quotes get a clear beat before them and land as someone else's words, not the narrator's own.
Pace: MEASURED and unhurried. THIS IS A TWO MINUTE PIECE, about one hundred and twenty seconds, and the read must FILL it, so give every sentence room to land and take a real breath at every period. Do not rush the numbers. Vary the tone line to line so no two sentences sound the same.

lines.text: There's a spot behind a salmon's eye the size of a pea.
lines.why: Opens curious and specific, not grand; the tiny precise detail is the pull.

lines.text: Hit it exactly and the fish dies instantly. [short pause] The flesh stays firm days longer.
lines.why: Lifts into the stakes of precision; the pause lets the payoff clause land separately.

lines.text: The Japanese call it EE-kay JEE-may. Spike the brain, bleed it, take the spinal cord.
lines.why: Settles into plain, informative mechanism after the stakes lift; contrast down.

lines.text: It's a hand skill that takes years. Almost nobody on a small boat has it.
lines.why: Grounded, a little slower on the rarity of the skill; sets up why a robot is needed.

lines.text: So a company, SHIN-kay Systems, built a robot to do it.
lines.why: The pivot to the company gets a small lift, forward motion into the mechanism story.

lines.text: Here's the part that's actually hard. [curious] The spot moves.
lines.why: Drops to set up the twist quietly before the founder quote; curious cue on the turn itself.

lines.text: Their founder put it plainly. [short pause]
lines.why: Quote lead-in, level and clean; the trailing pause is the beat before quoted speech begins.

lines.text: Even in the same species, even with the same contour, the brain can be in a different location.
lines.why: Read as someone else's words, given real weight; this is the founder's own claim and the crux of the mechanism.

lines.text: So you can't build a jig.
lines.why: Sharp drop after the quote; the conclusion lands flat and dry, not shouted.

lines.text: A jig only works when the target never moves.
lines.why: Rebuilding explanation, even and unhurried, climbing back toward the payoff.

lines.text: This one has to look at each fish and decide.
lines.why: Climbing energy into the Act One peak; 'decide' is the load-bearing word.

lines.text: That's the machine learning. Not the spike. [short pause] The looking.
lines.why: The genuine 'huh' beat that closes Act One; the pause isolates 'The looking' as the punchline.

lines.text: On July thirtieth, the company said it's bringing a smaller one to Alaska's Cook Inlet.
lines.why: New act begins on a clear drop from the peak; the announcement itself, even and clear.

lines.text: Nearly sixty percent smaller, they say. The robot's free, and they buy your fish at a premium.
lines.why: Stat line, don't rush the numbers; slight lift on the surprising claim of free plus premium.

lines.text: How much? [wry] There's no number anywhere.
lines.why: Dry, not snide, closing Act Two on the lowest energy so far; the wry cue keeps it light, not bitter.

lines.text: The fair case for patience.
lines.why: Act Three opens with real warmth, the thesis stated plainly and evenly.

lines.text: Every real pilot starts here. One boat, one write up.
lines.why: Building warmly on the fair case, a little brighter, crediting the normal shape of a pilot.

lines.text: Their C T O said it. [short pause]
lines.why: Second quote lead-in, quiet and level; the pause is the beat before quoted speech.

lines.text: Our technology only matters if it works in the environments where people actually fish.
lines.why: The warm peak of Act Three, read as the CTO's own words with genuine weight, not sarcasm.

lines.text: So fleet numbers on day one isn't fair.
lines.why: Settles back down from the quote, still warm, granting the fair point plainly.

lines.text: But you can ask what's on the water.
lines.why: The turn toward scrutiny; direct and a little firmer, but not accusatory.

lines.text: This week, one trade write up carries the whole Alaska story.
lines.why: Level, matter-of-fact statement of the actual evidence base, no editorializing in the tone.

lines.text: No Alaska outlet has touched it. [short pause] No boat count.
lines.why: Names the limits level and unsmug, per the brief; the pause separates the two absences cleanly.

lines.text: In twenty twenty four, their own goal was ten machines, company wide.
lines.why: First scale stat of Act Four, given room, not rushed.

lines.text: Upper Cook Inlet holds more than thirteen hundred salmon permits.
lines.why: The scale gap lands hardest here; brightest energy of the closing act to let the number register.

lines.text: About a tenth of every permit in Alaska.
lines.why: A sobering, quieter restatement of scale right after the big number, letting it sink in.

lines.text: And every one is a different boat. Different deck, different rail.
lines.why: Texture and specificity lift the energy back up before the turn into the button.

lines.text: The brain was the hard problem, and it's solved. [short pause]
lines.why: The turn drops to quiet certainty; the pause is the beat before the final line.

lines.text: The boat is the one still out there.
lines.why: The quietest, most open energy in the whole piece; lands plain and unresolved, not triumphant.
